```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import numpy as np

# ── Brand palette ──────────────────────────────────────
NAVY    = "#002E5D"
STEEL   = "#7A8D9C"
LIGHT   = "#D1D8DE"
ACCENT  = "#3A7CA5"
BG      = "#FAFBFC"
WHITE   = "#FFFFFF"
MUTED   = "#B0BEC5"

def brand_style(fig, ax):
    """Apply consistent McKinsey-style formatting."""
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(BG)
    ax.set_facecolor(BG)
    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['left'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['bottom'].set_color(LIGHT)
    ax.tick_params(colors=STEEL, labelsize=13)
    ax.yaxis.set_tick_params(length=0)
    ax.xaxis.set_tick_params(length=0)
    return fig, ax
```

## You do a lot strategy work and communication

Here's where you spend your time.

```{python}
#| label: fig-time-spent
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.2

categories = [
    "Technical",
    "Launch",
    "Analytics",
    "Execution",
    "Research",
    "Communication",
    "Strategy",
]
values = [6, 13, 19, 25, 38, 75, 75]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.2))
brand_style(fig, ax)

colors = [NAVY if v >= 60 else STEEL if v >= 30 else LIGHT for v in values]
bars = ax.barh(categories, values, color=colors, height=0.6, edgecolor="none")

for bar, val in zip(bars, values):
    ax.text(
        bar.get_width() + 1, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2,
        f"{val}%",
        va="center", ha="left",
        fontsize=13, fontweight="600",
        color=NAVY if val >= 60 else STEEL,
    )

ax.set_xlim(0, 100)
ax.set_xlabel("")
ax.set_xticks([])
ax.set_title(
    '% who spend "a lot" or "most of my time"',
    fontsize=12, color=STEEL, loc="left", pad=12, fontstyle="italic",
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: notes
"Heavy" = answered "A lot" or "Most of my time." The drop-off after research is steep. Only 3 of 16 spend heavy time on analytics, and just 1 on technical work.
:::

```{=html}
      <text x="464" y="232" font-size="13" fill="#002E5D" font-weight="700" font-family="'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif" letter-spacing="0.6">CODE</text>

    </svg>
  </div>

  <!-- ════════ RIGHT: Descriptions ════════ -->
  <div style="flex: 1; position: relative; height: 480px;">

    <!-- Layer 0: LLM -->
    <div class="pyramid-card" style="top: 28px;">
      <div class="pyramid-badge" style="background: linear-gradient(135deg, #e2e8ee, #ced8e0); color: #002E5D;">LLM</div>
      <div class="pyramid-desc">
        Text in, text out. Powerful, but can only <em>talk</em>.
        <span class="pyramid-example">"Write me a PRD" → get text back</span>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Layer 1: System Access -->
    <div class="pyramid-card" style="top: 130px; border-color: #c8d3dc;">
      <div class="pyramid-badge" style="background: linear-gradient(135deg, #8da0b0, #6d8a9e); color: #fff;">SYSTEM</div>
      <div class="pyramid-desc">
        Reads &amp; writes files, runs commands on <strong>your machine</strong>.
        <span class="pyramid-example">Navigate repos, install packages, manage git</span>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Layer 2: Code Execution -->
    <div class="pyramid-card" style="top: 235px; border-color: #b0cad8;">
      <div class="pyramid-badge" style="background: linear-gradient(135deg, #4a90b8, #2a6a90); color: #fff;">CODE</div>
      <div class="pyramid-desc">
        Writes code <em>and runs it</em> — tries, fails, fixes, retries.
        <span class="pyramid-example">Analyze a CSV, build a chart, debug an error</span>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Layer 3: Tools & Artifacts -->
    <div class="pyramid-card" style="top: 335px; border-color: #94b3ca;">
      <div class="pyramid-badge" style="background: linear-gradient(135deg, #0e3f6a, #001e3d); color: #fff;">TOOLS</div>
      <div class="pyramid-desc">
        Creates real deliverables &amp; connects to services.
        <span class="pyramid-example"><code>.docx</code> <code>.pptx</code> <code>.xlsx</code> · full apps · deploy to prod</span>
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
```

::: notes
The iceberg analogy: most people only interact with the tip (the LLM via a chat interface). Agents like Claude Code operate across all four layers. The deep layers are where the "unlock" capabilities live — data analysis, prototyping, artifact creation. This is what makes PMs into builders.
:::

:::

## What you'll build today {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

### Exercise 1: Get set up

Install VS Code and Claude Code, run your first prompt, and get comfortable with the terminal. By the end, everyone will have a working environment.

<br>

### Exercise 2: Write a PRD with AI

Use Claude Code to draft a product requirements document from a brief. You'll see how AI amplifies the spec writing you already do — faster first drafts, sharper acceptance criteria, structured output.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

### Exercise 3: Analyze data with AI

Load a real dataset into Claude Code and ask it questions. Build charts, find patterns, and generate a summary report — no SQL or Python experience needed.

<br>

### Exercise 4: Build a prototype

Take an idea from concept to working prototype using Claude Code. You'll have a live, interactive app running on your laptop by the end of the session.

:::
::::

::: notes
Exercises 1–2 are morning. Exercises 3–4 are afternoon. Each builds on the previous. Exercise 1 is amplify (what they already do). Exercises 3–4 are unlock (new capabilities).
:::
